plates.title: Screen hierarchy and safe interaction
notes: WORLD: large scene, four neutral hiding spots. Keep the full scene below the quest header.
HUD: quest + audio replay, 3-star counter, pause. Tools sit at the bottom safe area.
INITIAL: no animal, scissors, tail, ear, shadow or species sound is visible. Source star count must be corrected to 3.
MASTER FRAME: 1600 x 900. See layout.json for component rectangles; do not stretch the source bitmap.

plates.title: Quest header: no image answer leak
notes: Copy: Find a cat. Audio reads exactly the same quest. Keep sentence case.
Never add a cat thumbnail, silhouette, meow or answer-specific sparkle beside the instruction.
Replay button: 64 x 64 design units; at least 48 CSS px after scaling on a real device.
Target text is allowed. Discovering its visual meaning is the point of the level.

plates.title: Stars and scoring
notes: Begin at 3 / 3. Only a wrong YES / NO answer loses one star.
No penalty for opening a distractor, missing a swipe, choosing another tool or taking time.
Clamp at zero. Continue with guided help; no negative scores and no forced restart.
One charge per reveal. Completing with 1 star displays and saves 1 star, not 3.

plates.title: Hiding layers and object visibility
notes: This crop shows a REVEALED cat; it is NOT a valid starting background.
Runtime layers: empty background -> object (invisible) -> closed cover -> reveal VFX.
Switch the object visible only at reveal completion. Disable its input before that point.
Every spot uses the same idle motion distribution, independent of its occupant.

plates.title: Swipe Leaves interaction
notes: Select leaves tool; drag the cover sideways. Accumulate signed displacement, not back-and-forth rubbing.
Threshold: 55% of cover width, capped at 96 design units. Release below threshold springs back.
0-180 ms: cover follows gesture. 180-520 ms: leaves part. 520-820 ms: neutral reveal and quiz.
Tap-to-open alternative is available. Wrong gesture is never a learning error.

plates.title: Throw Net interaction
notes: Select net; tap a compatible bush. Use a deterministic arc to the chosen spot.
0-360 ms: cast. 360-620 ms: net catches foliage. 620-900 ms: lift and dissolve net.
Reveal the animal AFTER the net disappears. Never show an animal bound in the net.
Lock other spots during the short reveal animation; then open the quiz.

plates.title: Blast Berry interaction
notes: Select foam berry; tap a rock cover. Aim preview is neutral and not tied to the answer.
0-280 ms: berry arc. 280-560 ms: soft puff and split rock. 560-1000 ms: debris fades, reveal.
No realistic explosion, sharp shards, injury or damage to a visible object or animal.
Keep this effect deterministic with tweens. Full destruction physics is unnecessary.

plates.title: Question panel and input lock
notes: Question: Is this a cat? Show ONLY the revealed object portrait beside it.
Before an answer: no object name, green outline, success audio or correctness hint.
YES and NO are equal-sized controls. Remove the X while the question is unanswered.
While the panel is active, the world and tool tray cannot receive input.

plates.title: Correct NO on a distractor
notes: Reveal: dog. Quest: Find a cat. Child chooses NO.
Feedback: No. It is a dog. Keep all current stars.
Mark this spot searched, remove its quiz trigger and return to searching.
This NEVER completes the level. Momo encourages the child to find the cat.

plates.title: Correct YES on the target
notes: Reveal: cat. Quest: Find a cat. Child chooses YES.
Feedback: Yes! It is a cat. Set completion state exactly once.
Play greeting and celebration; retain remaining stars. Offer Next and Play again.
Never reuse the source storyboard caption saying to continue searching after this answer.

plates.title: Wrong answer and assisted retry
notes: Wrong YES on dog: lose one star; show No. It is a dog.; return to search.
Wrong NO on cat: lose one star; explain Yes. It is a cat.; offer an assisted YES retry.
Repeated NO on that same revealed cat does not drain more stars. No extra learning credit.
Use atomic processing, revealId and answerEventId to reject duplicate taps and retries.

plates.title: Success pose and payoff
notes: Target + YES is the only success gate. Searching all spots is not itself a win.
Momo and the found animal meet. Gentle sparkles, a brief voice cue, then stable result UI.
No intense flash or unavoidable shaking. Reduced motion uses fades.
Stars shown in the reference are illustrative; runtime must use the current session value.

plates.title: Tool tray and mobile ergonomics
notes: Desktop: three tools centred at the bottom. Highlight the selected TOOL, never the hidden answer.
Mobile landscape: compact floating tray, minimum 48 CSS px per control and safe-area offsets.
Tap tool -> tap spot is sufficient. Drag precision is optional.
Unsupported tool on a spot: a neutral bounce and tool hint; no penalty.

plates.title: Objects, plural grammar and feedback
notes: Level one distractors: dog, tiger and scissors. All use the same question: Is this a cat?
If the target is scissors, use Find the scissors. and Are these scissors?
Scissors are one vocabulary entity despite plural grammar. Store complete authored sentences.
Do not generate articles or plural questions with simple string concatenation.

plates.title: Art handoff and export boundaries
notes: These are detailed crops from two flattened concept images, not rigged or transparent game sprites.
Do not put the whole concept image under invisible click zones. It contains answer leaks.
Separate empty scenery, covers, objects, Momo frames and UI text before shipping.
Asset production checklist names every missing runtime texture and animation frame.
